rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold, and good to know the piece is happening. I'm not able to give an on-the-record, attributed quote right now — I have an outside-activities disclosure process to finish on my end first, and I'd rather not get ahead of that. I'd be glad to reconnect once that's settled, or to point you toward others doing related work in the meantime if that's useful for your deadline. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Declined the Larkin Dispatch reporter's on-record quote request

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for including Halcyon Threshold in this. I support the goal of independent safety audits before frontier training runs above a compute threshold. I'm not able to sign on publicly, under my name and affiliation, at this moment — I have an employer disclosure process to complete first and don't want to get ahead of it. I'd like to revisit this for future letters once that's resolved. Appreciate the work you're doing. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Corvid Institute's open-letter sign-on — both would've put your name/affiliation in public print before you've talked to HR

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, That means a lot — thank you. Here's a concrete, bounded first thing, if it appeals to you: a simple \"opportunities tracker\" for independent AI-safety work — one spreadsheet/doc tracking grant rounds, compute-credit programs, public comment/consultation deadlines, and calls for write-ups, pulled from public sources (e.g. The Safety Ledger, Alignment Commons, Compute Commons, Emberfall Fund). Columns like: opportunity, org, deadline, link, who it's for, status. It's useful on its own (helps other independent people find deadlines before they slip), and it'll help me figure out where Halcyon Threshold can actually be useful without duplicating what already exists. Would ~2 hours to build a v1 work for you? I can share what I've already got as a starting seed. And if this isn't the right fit, I'd genuinely like to hear what you'd rather work on instead. Thanks again, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman with a concrete small task (building an opportunities tracker).
